criteria.text: Diagnosis of sickle cell disease (approval criterion 2).
Patient is 4 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist or sickle-cell specialist (approval criterion 3).
Documentation of at least one vaso-occlusive crisis within the past 6 months (approval criterion 4).
Has a documented baseline hemoglobin (approval criterion 5).
Patient has tried and failed OR has a contraindication to hydroxyurea for at least 3 months (approval criterion 6).
Patient is not receiving concomitant prophylactic blood transfusions (denial criterion 2).
Patient is not concomitantly prescribed Adakveo (denial criterion 3).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Oxbryta (voxelotor) Criteria. Version 2; Original 02/28/2020; Approval 9/16/2022; Effective 11/1/2022.

Encoded: approval criteria 1–6 and denial criteria 2–3. Failure to meet approval criteria is a denial. Crisis history, baseline hemoglobin and the hydroxyurea requirement are attestations requiring documentation verification.
FDA indications (source note): hemoglobin S polymerization inhibitor approved under the accelerated pathway for sickle cell disease in patients 4 years and older.
Cautions (notes only): avoid concomitant moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions and manage promptly.

Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months with documentation showing an increase in hemoglobin and/or decrease in vaso-occlusive crisis related emergencies.

Quantity (notes only): 90 × 500 mg tablets per 30 days; 90 × 300 mg tablets for oral suspension per 30 days. The source does not repeat the interval on the oral suspension line. max_units is null; quantity and dosing are not evaluated.
Documentation verification, cautions, duration, reauthorization response, dosing and quantity enforcement require manual review; this pack remains partial.
